disclaimer: Recreational and educational trainer. Not for operational aviation use. Confirm the current Czech AIP before any real flight.

geography.method: OSM API 0.6 map extract of the LKPR area, filtered to aeroway features and saved in data/lkpr_aeroway.geojson. Rebuild with scripts/build_lkpr_data.py.
simplified_or_unverified: The diagram is drawn from OSM centre-lines and area outlines, not from the official aerodrome chart AD 2-LKPR-2-1.
OSM runway 06/24 centre-line length is about 3708 m. AIP AD 2.12 publishes 3715 m.
A 67 m taxiway link between A1 and Z has no ref and no name in OSM. The trainer does not invent a designator for it.

The holding point is an OSM node (holding_position:type=runway) on taxiway Z, about 131 m from the runway 06/24 centre-line. AIP AD 2.20.4.5 says a CAT I holding point for runway 24 is on taxiway Z. This trainer does not claim the OSM node is that surveyed coordinate.
Stand 3 coordinates are the OSM parking-position lead-in. AIP lists stand 3 among visual-docking stands but does not publish this coordinate.
Pushback is drawn along that lead-in line. No pushback facing was published for this scenario, so none is invented.

aip.source: Czech Aeronautical Information Publication, Václav Havel Airport Praha/Ruzyně, AD 2 LKPR
aip.runway_preference_reference: AD 2.21.2.1. The trainer uses runway 24 because it is first in that published order, not because of live wind or ATIS.
aip.movement: AD 2.20.2.3: instructions that direct aircraft movement are issued by RUZYNĚ GROUND or RUZYNĚ TOWER, depending on the hours in AD 2.18.

frequencies.remarks: English only. Outside these hours contact Ruzyně Tower 134.560. ATC clearance is also available as DCL via ACARS.

simulated: QNH 1013 hPa is the standard-pressure training value. It is not a METAR, ATIS, or local QNH.
No ATIS information letter is simulated.
No SID, flight-planned route, squawk, or initial-climb altitude is issued. Those depend on the actual flight and are not invented here.
Callsign OK-ABC / Oscar Kilo Alfa Bravo Charlie is a fictional training registration.
The taxi instruction 'via Alfa one and Zulu' is a training clearance along one path in the OSM taxiway graph. It is not a published standard taxi route.
Calling Delivery for runway and QNH, then Ground for startup and pushback, is a simplified training flow. It is labeled as such and is not a transcript of local phraseology.
When the departure handoff is given, and the exact wording of each transmission, is training design based on ICAO-style readback practice.
Aircraft speed on the diagram is sped up so the exercise stays short. Apron speed limits in the AIP are not modelled.
phraseology: Readback items follow the usual ICAO mandatory-readback set (runway, hold short, line up and wait, takeoff clearance, altimeter, frequency change). This is training design, not a local phraseology exam.
